# Purpose and scope

The production bioreactor is the step at which the glycan, charge variant and aggregate
quality attributes of A-Mab are formed. The purification train that follows carries those
attributes through with little modification, and no step downstream of the harvest reforms
a glycan or reverses a deamidation. For this reason the bioreactor is the step at which the
design space for product quality is defined, and this plan sets out the studies that will
define it.

The commercial process operates at `{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L of culture, a scale at which
the number of runs a designed experiment needs cannot be supplied, and the studies will
therefore be executed on a qualified scale-down model of that vessel. The plan states what
will be studied, how the study will be run and how the results will be judged. The findings
themselves belong to the paired report (PCR-003) and are not anticipated here.

The scope covers the `{python} n_par` process parameters of the production bioreactor
listed in @tbl-params, the `{python} n_resp` quality attributes that will be measured as
responses, and the analytical methods that support them. The work is a Stage 1 process
design activity in the sense of the lifecycle approach [@fda2011], carried out under the
enhanced development approach [@ichq8; @ichq11], and criticality is treated throughout as a
continuum and not as a binary split into critical and non-critical attributes [@ichq9].
Seed expansion up to the N-1 stage lies outside the scope, since prior platform knowledge
covers it and PTP-001 records that position. The same scope excludes harvest and
clarification, which PCP-004 covers.

Two limits apply to this plan. The first limit is that it does not qualify the scale-down
model, which is qualified under SOP-1001 and reported separately. The second limit is that
it does not by itself define the commercial control strategy, because host cell protein and
residual DNA are formed in the bioreactor and cleared by later steps (PCP-005, PCP-007 and
PCP-008).

# Objectives

The study has five objectives, and each one produces a defined output in PCR-003 and a
defined input to the control strategy the transfer will hand to the receiving site.

(i) Quantify the effect of each parameter in @tbl-params on the `{python} n_resp` quality
attributes the production bioreactor forms, over ranges deliberately wider than the ranges
the commercial process will use, and estimate the interactions between the parameters
studied together.

(ii) Define a multivariate operating region in the well-controlled culture parameters over
which every attribute the step governs is predicted to meet acceptance, and locate the
normal operating ranges of @tbl-params inside that region.

(iii) Establish a proven acceptable range for each parameter that governs an attribute,
under both of the analyses described in §8, and state for each range the acceptance
criterion it was judged against.

(iv) Classify every parameter as a critical, well-controlled critical, key or general
process parameter, using the decision logic of SOP-4001 together with the control
capability the receiving site can demonstrate for that parameter.

(v) Provide the ranges, the in-process controls and the monitoring commitments that the
Stage 2 control strategy will carry for this step, with the evidence for each of them.

Objectives (i) to (iii) rest on the designed experiments in §6, while objective (iv) rests
on those experiments together with the equipment capability the transfer confirms.
Objective (v) is the output the transfer needs, and the first four objectives support it.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge

A-Mab is produced by fed-batch culture of a recombinant Chinese hamster ovary cell line in
a stirred tank bioreactor. The culture is inoculated from the N-1 seed bioreactor, held at
set-points for pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen and dissolved CO2, and fed on a fixed
schedule until the harvest criterion is met. Operation follows SOP-2003, and medium and
feed are prepared under SOP-2004.

The platform is not new: three earlier humanized IgG1 products (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab)
have been manufactured on it at commercial scale, and A-Mab itself has been produced
through clinical supply and through engineering runs. That experience establishes the
mechanisms the study expects to see. The study therefore confirms and bounds behaviour at
this step instead of discovering it. Several A-Mab acceptance limits were themselves set
from X-Mab clinical experience on the same platform. Therefore, the platform is the source
of some of the acceptance criteria as well as of the mechanistic expectations.

Three of the five modelled attributes are enzymatic in origin: galactosylation, high
mannose and afucosylation. Galactosylation follows the activity of the Golgi
galactosyltransferase and the supply of the nucleotide sugar donor, both of which decline
as a culture ages and the intracellular environment deteriorates. High mannose reports how
completely mannosidase trimming has run, which makes the attribute sensitive to lumenal pH
and to temperature (the two parameters that set enzyme activity most directly).
Afucosylation is the one attribute of the three set by a competition, between core
fucosyltransferase activity and the rate at which antibody leaves the Golgi, and the level
is expected to fall as a culture is extended.

The other two modelled attributes are chemical in origin, and both are expected to depend
on culture duration more than on any other parameter. Acidic charge variants arise mainly
from deamidation of product already secreted into the broth, which proceeds faster at
higher pH and accumulates over a longer culture. Aggregate has the same character, because
antibody that sits longer in an ageing broth aggregates more. Both expectations point at
culture duration as the parameter to bound. They are tested and quantified by the designed
experiments in §6.

## Quality attributes in scope

The quality attributes the production bioreactor sets are listed in @tbl-cqa with the
acceptance criterion and the criticality of each, and the score in the last column is the
Tool #1 impact and uncertainty score of the A-Mab risk methodology [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print()
print(": Quality attributes set by the production bioreactor. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

The highest score of the seven attributes in @tbl-cqa belongs to high mannose, at
`{python} f"{cq.loc['High Mannose','Tool #1']:.0f}"`, which is also the only one of very
high criticality. Afucosylation and galactosylation follow, both of high criticality and
both linked to the effector function that carries the mechanism of action. The same
criticality applies to aggregates, which are the one attribute in the group that a later
step reduces (PCP-007). Acidic charge variants sit at the other end of the register at
`{python} f"{cq.loc['Acidic charge variants (deamidation)','Tool #1']:.0f}"`, of very low
criticality, and enter the study because the culture conditions move them and not because
the drug substance is at risk from them.

Host cell protein and residual DNA are the two attributes formed in the bioreactor that are
not modelled here, although both will be measured in the harvest of every run, because the
load the purification train receives is an input to the clearance claims in PCR-005,
PCR-007 and PCR-008. The `{python} n_resp` attributes that are modelled are the ones this
step both forms and hands on unchanged.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters

RA-001 set the scope of this study, scoring each parameter on the potential impact of
variation on a quality attribute and on the potential for interaction with other
parameters, and deriving a study type from the combined score [@amab2009]. Of the
`{python} n_par` parameters in @tbl-params, `{python} n_mv` were assigned to the
multivariate design and `{python} n_uv` to univariate assessment, and this plan executes
that assignment without revisiting it.

The `{python} n_mv` multivariate parameters are culture pH, culture temperature, dissolved
CO2, osmolality and culture duration, and each of them has a mechanism on at least one
glycan or charge attribute together with a plausible interaction with at least one of the
others. Culture pH and culture temperature act on the same enzymatic steps, which is the
clearest interaction the design has to resolve. Culture duration multiplies the exposure of
every attribute to the conditions the other four parameters set, which makes an interaction
with duration plausible in each case.

The `{python} n_uv` univariate parameters are dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell
concentration, basal medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume, and these four act on
cell growth and on process performance, where platform experience across the three earlier
products shows the effect on product quality to be small over the ranges proposed. A
univariate assessment is adequate where a parameter has no plausible interaction with the
multivariate set, and RA-001 found none for these four.

The ranges in @tbl-params are the knowledge space and not the operating ranges, and each
characterization range spans `{python} f"{w_lo:.1f}"` to `{python} f"{w_hi:.1f}"` times the
width of the matching normal operating range. The extra width serves two purposes. It puts
real distance between the design edges and the range the plant will use, which is what
turns an effect estimate into a bound on operation. In addition, it leaves room for later
process improvement inside a region that has already been studied [@amab2009]. No range
extends into conditions under which the culture is known to fail.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

Execution will use bench-scale stirred tank bioreactors of equivalent design to the
commercial vessels, operated under SOP-2003. The scale-independent parameters (pH,
temperature, dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration and culture duration) will
be set to the values the commercial process uses. The scale-dependent parameters
(agitation, gas flow rates, headspace pressure and working volume) will be set so that the
bench system matches commercial process performance. Matching the commercial hardware
settings themselves would not reproduce the culture environment, because the relation
between an agitation rate and the shear a cell experiences changes with vessel geometry.

Qualification of the model is a precondition of execution and is not part of this study,
and SOP-1001 governs it. Execution will not begin until the qualification report is
approved. The qualification compares the bench system with `{python} f"{scale_l:,}"` L data
on the inputs and the outputs that matter here: the growth and viability profile, the titer
and the `{python} n_resp` modelled attributes. A model that fails qualification for one
attribute may still be used for the others, provided PCR-003 states the restriction.

The centre-point replicates in each design serve two purposes. They provide the pure error
term against which lack of fit is tested (§5.5), and they show whether the bench system
reproduces the set-point condition across the campaign. `{python} cp_scr` centre points are
included in the screening design and `{python} cp_rsm` in the response-surface design.

## Cell line, media and culture operation

The cell line is the recombinant Chinese hamster ovary line used for A-Mab clinical supply,
drawn from the qualified working cell bank, and basal medium and feed are chemically
defined and prepared under SOP-2004. One lot of medium and one lot of feed will serve the
whole campaign, which keeps lot variation out of the designed experiments.

Each run will be inoculated at the initial viable cell concentration the design specifies,
controlled to the pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen and dissolved CO2 set-points of that
run, and fed on the platform schedule until the harvest day the design specifies. Daily
samples support process monitoring, and the harvest sample supports the quality attributes.

Inputs held to platform specification are identity tested and quality controlled, and they
are not characterized in this study: medium and feed lots, the gas supply and the working
cell bank all fall in that group. A change to any input in that group changes the material
basis of the study, and it would be assessed under change control before execution
continued.

## Analytical methods

Released N-glycan mapping by 2-AB HILIC-UPLC (SOP-3010, AMV-3010) reports afucosylation,
galactosylation and high mannose from one chromatogram, size variants by SEC-HPLC
(SOP-3011, AMV-3011) report aggregates, and charge variants by imaged capillary isoelectric
focusing (SOP-3013, AMV-3013) report acidic variants. Host cell protein by ELISA
(AMV-3012) and residual host cell DNA by qPCR (AMV-3014) characterize the harvest load.

Method performance is not restated in this plan. The performance figures (precision,
accuracy and quantitation limits) are held in the validation reports named in @tbl-sop, and
PCR-003 will quote the relevant one wherever an effect approaches the precision of the
method. Where scheduling allows, samples from all runs of one design will be assayed in a
single analytical sequence, and every sequence carries a control sample, because drift
between sequences would enter the model as run to run variation.

## Sampling plan

One harvest sample per run is the primary sample of this study. It will be taken at the
culture duration the run specifies, clarified by the standard bench procedure and split for
the assays in §5.3. Sample handling, labelling and storage follow SOP-2003.

Daily in-process samples will be taken for viable cell density, viability and the main
metabolites (for example glucose and lactate), and these support the interpretation of the
harvest result and confirm that a run behaved as the design intended. They are not
modelled.

In both designs, the centre-point runs carry the replicate structure. All of them are run
at the set-points in @tbl-params, `{python} cp_scr` of them in the screening design and
`{python} cp_rsm` in the response-surface design. Centre points will be scheduled at the
start of each execution block, in the middle and at the end, and a drift over the campaign
will then appear as a difference between replicates.

## Statistical methods

Analysis follows SOP-1002, and the factors are coded so that the set-point is zero and the
edges of the characterization range are −1 and +1. The coded factors put every effect on
one scale, which is the change in the response across half the studied range [@amab2009].
Effects are reported in the natural units of the response.

The screening design will be analysed by ordinary least squares, with all main effects and
all two-factor interactions in the model, and an effect is twice the coefficient on the
coded factor, because one coded unit is half the characterization range. Every term in that
model is assessed at α = 0.05.

The response-surface design will be analysed with a full quadratic model in the retained
factors, comprising the main effects, the two-factor interactions and the pure quadratic
terms. The adequacy of that model will be judged on R², on the adjusted and predicted forms
of R², on the overall F test and on an analysis of variance that partitions the residual
into lack of fit and pure error. The predicted form is computed from PRESS residuals, which
makes it a check on prediction and not on fit, while pure error comes from the centre-point
replicates alone, which is why the replicate count matters more here than the total run
count.

The two designs answer different questions: the screening design identifies which factors
matter, and the response-surface design is the predictive model from which the operating
region in PCR-003 will be derived. A screening model in `{python} n_scr_f` factors fitted
to `{python} n_scr` runs is close to saturated, and a high fit statistic from such a model
is not evidence of predictive quality.

For each attribute, capability will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of
`{python} f"{n_mc:,}"` batches. Each simulated batch draws every parameter inside the
normal operating range in @tbl-params, and the fitted response-surface model predicts each
attribute for it. Capability is reported as a one-sided Cpk against the governing limit,
with the margin to that limit. The Cpk estimate is conditioned on the scale-down model and on the fitted
model. It is not a commercial-scale measurement, and Stage 2 provides that confirmation
[@fda2011].

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and study type

The parameters, the set-points, the ranges to be studied, the normal operating ranges and
the study types are given in @tbl-params.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(plan_params(UO))
print()
print(": Parameters to be studied, with the range studied and the normal operating "
      "range. {#tbl-params}")
```

For the design matrices in Appendix A and Appendix B, the letter codes are given in
@tbl-legend.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Factor legend for the coded design matrices. {#tbl-legend}")
```

Culture pH will be studied over `{python} rng('pH')`, against a normal operating range of
`{python} nor('pH')`, and that width covers the excursions a commercial vessel can show
during a base addition into a large working volume. Culture temperature will be studied
over `{python} rng('temperature')` °C, which is wider than the control system is capable of
drifting. Osmolality will be studied over `{python} rng('osmolality')` mOsm, which covers
the rise a full feed schedule produces. Dissolved CO2 will be studied over
`{python} rng('co2')` mmHg, because CO2 accumulates at large scale and a commercial vessel
is expected to sit higher than a bench vessel held at the same set-point [@amab2009].
Culture duration will be studied over `{python} rng('duration')` days, which brackets the
platform harvest day on both sides. The `{python} n_uv` univariate parameters will be
studied over the ranges in the same table, one at a time (§6.4).

## Screening design

The screening design is a two-level fractional factorial in the `{python} n_scr_f` factors,
with `{python} n_fact_scr` factorial runs and `{python} cp_scr` centre points,
`{python} n_scr` runs in all, against the `{python} n_full_scr` runs a full factorial in
those factors would need. The fractional design is of resolution V. Therefore, the design
estimates every main effect clear of every two-factor interaction, and it aliases each
two-factor interaction only with a three-factor interaction. The planned matrix is given in
Appendix A.

At the screening stage, three-factor and higher interactions are assumed to be negligible,
an assumption that is standard at that stage and that platform experience gives no reason
to doubt for this step. However, a fractional design of this kind cannot resolve every
interaction, and the factors it retains go forward into the response-surface stage for
that reason.

The screening stage identifies. It does not define an operating region, and PCR-003 will
not present a screening fit as a predictive model.

## Response-surface design

The response-surface design is a face-centred central composite in the
`{python} n_rsm_f` factors that screening is expected to retain: culture pH, culture
temperature, culture duration and dissolved CO2. It comprises `{python} n_fact_rsm`
factorial runs, `{python} n_ax_rsm` axial runs and `{python} cp_rsm` centre points,
`{python} n_rsm` runs in all. The axial runs sit on the faces of the cube, at the edges of
the characterization ranges, and a rotatable design would place them outside the ranges
@tbl-params defines. Consequently, no run in this study leaves the knowledge space.

The second stage exists for curvature, because a two-level design cannot separate a curved
response from a linear one and the centre points of the screening design can show only that
curvature is present. The planned matrix is given in Appendix B.

Although the matrix in Appendix B assumes that screening retains the four factors named
above, screening may retain a different set, and the matrix will then be re-issued before
execution. A re-issue on that ground is an amendment to this plan and not a deviation from
it.

## Univariate assessment

The `{python} n_uv` univariate parameters are dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell
concentration, basal medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume, and each of the four
will be assessed separately, at the low edge of the characterization range, at the
set-point and at the high edge. While one parameter moves, the other three and all
`{python} n_mv` multivariate factors are held at the set-points in @tbl-params.

By construction, a univariate assessment cannot detect an interaction between the parameter
it moves and the parameters it holds, and that limitation is accepted here on the basis of
RA-001, which found no plausible interaction between these four parameters and the
multivariate set.
However, should a univariate result contradict that finding, the parameter will be carried
into a multivariate follow-up study and PCR-003 will record the decision.

# Acceptance and decision criteria

The criteria below are fixed before execution, because a criterion agreed after the results
are known describes them instead of testing them.

The scale-down model is acceptable when the qualification under SOP-1001 shows no
statistically significant difference between scales in the growth profile, the titer and
the `{python} n_resp` modelled attributes. Execution of the study begins once that
qualification report is approved.

A factor is carried from screening into the response-surface stage when a main effect, or
an interaction containing it, reaches significance at α = 0.05 for at least one attribute.
A factor may also be carried on mechanistic grounds, where the estimated effect is of the
same order as the significant terms and the residual degrees of freedom are few, and any
factor carried on that second ground will be identified as such in PCR-003.

A response-surface model is adequate for the operating region when the overall regression
is significant at α = 0.05, when the adjusted and predicted forms of R² are consistent with
each other and when the lack-of-fit test is not significant against pure error. However, a
model that fails the lack-of-fit test may still support a restricted region, and PCR-003
will state the restriction and the reason for it. Where a lack of fit cannot be resolved by
reducing the model or by restricting the region, the study has failed for that attribute,
and the attribute is then held by monitoring and by release testing until further work is
completed.

The operating region is acceptable when every attribute the step governs is predicted to
meet the criterion in §8 throughout the region, including at the corner where the
prediction is least favourable. The normal operating ranges in @tbl-params must lie inside
the region with margin, and if they do not, the operating ranges will be narrowed and the
criterion will not be relaxed to accommodate them.

At the end of the study, every parameter will be given a class under SOP-4001: critical
process parameter, well-controlled critical process parameter, key process parameter or
general process parameter. The class follows from the demonstrated effect on a quality
attribute and from the risk that the parameter leaves the region during commercial operation [@amab2009]. A
parameter with no significant effect is still classified, and the absence of an effect is
kept in the knowledge space as evidence of robustness over the ranges studied.

No numeric capability threshold is set in this plan. Capability will be reported for each
attribute as a one-sided Cpk with the margin to the limit, and the acceptability of the set
is judged in PCMR-001 against the framework in PCMP-001. A capability estimated from a
scale-down model is a prediction, and confirmation at commercial scale is a Stage 2
activity [@fda2011].

Any departure from this plan during execution will be recorded, investigated and impact
assessed, and PCR-003 will carry the assessment. A deviation that invalidates a run
requires that run to be repeated before the affected design is analysed.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis)

A proven acceptable range is the range of one parameter over which a quality attribute
stays within acceptance while the other parameters are held or varied in a stated way. The
range is univariate and the design space is multivariate. The design space and the ranges
are kept apart in PCR-003, and this section states in advance how each range is derived.

The criterion a range is judged against comes first. For each of the `{python} n_resp`
modelled attributes the criterion is the drug-substance specification in @tbl-cqa, unless a
tighter in-process limit applies to the bioreactor harvest itself. Two kinds of in-process
limit apply at this step. For the three glycan attributes and for acidic variants, none of
which the purification train clears or modifies, the limit will be set from the capability this
study demonstrates, at `{python} f"{alert_sigma:g}"` standard deviations from the mean. For
aggregates the limit is carried back from the drug-substance specification through the
clearance the downstream steps deliver, then divided by an assurance margin of
`{python} f"{agg_margin:g}"`. The analysis reads the applicable criterion for each
attribute from the register, and no criterion is calculated by hand.

For every pairing of an attribute with a response-surface factor, two analyses will be run.
The first holds the other factors at the set-points in @tbl-params and scans the parameter
of interest across the full characterization range, evaluating the fitted response-surface
model at `{python} par_grid` grid points. The second propagates normal operating variation:
at each of `{python} par_mc_grid` grid points the other factors are drawn within the normal
operating ranges in @tbl-params, `{python} f"{par_mc_n:,}"` draws at each point, with the
residual variance of the model added to every prediction.

The decision rule differs between the two analyses. Under the first, the proven acceptable
range is the contiguous interval containing the set-point over which the predicted mean
stays within acceptance. Under the second, the interval must hold the whole 95 % predictive
interval within acceptance. The second rule is a robustness criterion and will give the
narrower answer wherever the other factors have an effect. Both ranges will be reported for
every pairing, in one table.

Each governed attribute will also be presented as a figure against the parameter that
governs it, in two panels that correspond to the two analyses, with the acceptance limit
drawn, the acceptable region shaded green, and the set-point and the normal operating range
marked. Where a proven acceptable range covers the whole characterization range, the
parameter does not constrain the step over the region studied. The binding constraint on
the step is then the multivariate corner of the design space, and not any univariate range.

Every proven acceptable range this study reports will carry three bounds. Nothing is proven
outside the characterization range, because nothing outside it was studied. The range is a
property of the fitted response-surface model, and a model that fails the adequacy criteria
in §7 supports no proven acceptable range at all. Finally, the second analysis propagates
the normal operating variation of the other response-surface factors and the residual
variance of the model, and it does not propagate variation in the parameters assessed
univariately.

# Data management and integrity

Throughout the study, records will be attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original and
accurate, and they will also be complete, consistent, enduring and available (ALCOA+).

Raw analytical data are acquired and retained in the validated chromatography and
electrophoresis data systems, with audit trails enabled, and bioreactor process data are
acquired by the control system and retained in the process historian. The design matrices,
the calculated results and the statistical analyses are held in a version-controlled study
workbook, from which the analysis will be reproducible using the raw data and the recorded
model settings.

Before analysis, every transcription of a result will be verified by a second person. The
statistical analysis will be reviewed by someone other than the analyst who performed it.
Records are retained under the site record retention procedure.

# Roles and responsibilities

Process Development and MSAT own this plan. Process Development and MSAT also design the
study, execute the bioreactor runs, perform the statistical analysis and write PCR-003.

Analytical Development performs the assays in §5.3, maintains the validated methods and
reports the analytical results. Manufacturing Science reviews the design and the proposed
ranges against the capability of the commercial equipment, and confirms that the ranges the
study proposes can be held at the receiving site. Statistics reviews the design, the model
forms and the analysis. Quality Assurance approves this plan and PCR-003, and dispositions
any deviation raised during execution.

# Deliverables and schedule

The deliverable is PCR-003, the process characterization report for the production
bioreactor, which carries the effects, the models, the operating region, the proven
acceptable ranges, the capability estimates and the parameter classifications, and which
rolls up into PCMR-001.

The work runs in four phases, of which qualification of the scale-down model under SOP-1001
comes first, followed by execution and analysis of the screening design and then by
execution and analysis of the response-surface design. Once the analytical results for
every run of a phase are available, analysis of that phase begins. The univariate
assessments may run in parallel with either designed experiment. Because the campaign
schedule is held in PTP-001, no calendar dates are given here.

# Risks and assumptions

The principal risk to the study is that the scale-down model does not represent the
commercial vessel for the attributes being modelled, and dissolved CO2 is where that risk
concentrates, because CO2 accumulation depends on scale and a bench vessel strips it more
readily than a commercial one [@amab2009]. Including dissolved CO2 as a factor over
`{python} rng('co2')` mmHg is the mitigation, since the range covers the levels a
commercial vessel reaches whether or not the bench vessel reaches them by the same route.

Material supply is the second risk. Using one lot of medium and one lot of feed across the
campaign keeps lot variation out of the model, and it also means the study says nothing
about lot variation. That variation is handled by the incoming material specification and
by SOP-2004, and not by this study.

Assay variability is the third risk. Where an effect is small relative to the precision of
the method, PCR-003 will attribute the variability to the assay and will hedge the
conclusion accordingly. That variability is estimated from the centre-point replicates,
which give the combined process and assay term such a judgement needs.

Three assumptions are open to challenge and are stated here for that reason. Three-factor
and higher interactions are assumed negligible in the screening design. The model fitted to
the response-surface design is assumed to hold across the whole characterization region,
which the lack-of-fit test examines and cannot prove. Finally, the platform mechanisms in
§4.1 are assumed to apply to A-Mab, and the study confirms or refutes them for each of the five
modelled attributes.

# Approvals

This plan takes effect once the functions listed in @tbl-appr have approved it. Execution
begins after that approval and after the scale-down model qualification report is approved.
Any change before execution is complete will be issued as a revision of this plan and
approved by the same functions.
